students.name: Junainah
supplies_needed: 5 small cups + cotton balls + smell samples (vanilla, lemon, mint, cinnamon, coffee)
Taste samples (lemon, sugar, salt, dark chocolate)

daily_lessons.title: Sight & Hearing Mechanics
objectives: Identify receptor types in eyes and ears
Observe pupil response to light changes
Understand eardrum and cochlea vibrations
daily_lessons.instructions: Perform the pupil expansion experiment in front of a mirror with dim and bright light. Test sound vibrations using stretched rubber bands.

daily_lessons.title: Smell, Taste & Touch Pathways
objectives: Explain chemoreception in nasal passages and tongue
Debunk the tongue taste map myth (all areas detect 5 basic tastes)
Understand sensory neurons and reflex arcs
daily_lessons.instructions: Conduct a blindfolded smell identification test using 5 cups, followed by a 4-taste test on different parts of the tongue.

daily_lessons.title: The 7 Traits of Life (MRS GREN)
objectives: Master the MRS GREN acronym (Movement, Respiration, Sensitivity, Growth, Reproduction, Excretion, Nutrition)
Differentiate cellular respiration from breathing
daily_lessons.instructions: Create a detailed MRS GREN cheat sheet with examples for each characteristic.

daily_lessons.title: 3-Way Sorting Investigation
objectives: Categorize items into Living, Dead (once alive), and Non-Living
Analyze edge cases (e.g., wooden spoons, dried leaves, water, soil)
daily_lessons.instructions: Take a 20-minute indoor/outdoor walk and record at least 12 items in a 3-column chart.

daily_lessons.title: Deep Dive Research & Week 1 Quiz
objectives: Investigate a scientific anomaly (Viruses, Venus Flytraps, or Bat Echolocation)
Complete Week 1 Knowledge Assessment
daily_lessons.instructions: Write a 1-page report or record a short video on whether viruses are considered living or non-living, then take the quiz.

questions.question: What does the 'R' in MRS GREN stand for?
Which sensory receptors in the retina are responsible for seeing color?

students.name: Hessa
supplies_needed: 5 smell jars (vanilla, lemon, coffee, mint, cinnamon)
4 taste test items (lemon wedge, sugar water, salt water, dark chocolate)
Paper mystery bag + 6 tactile objects (sandpaper, sponge, key, pinecone, spoon, cotton)

daily_lessons.title: Sight - How Our Eyes Work
objectives: Name the eyes as the organ for sight
Observe how pupils change size in light and dark
daily_lessons.instructions: Look in the mirror in a dim room, then turn on the light and watch your pupils shrink!

daily_lessons.title: Hearing - Sound Vibrations
objectives: Identify ears as the organ for hearing
Feel vibrations created by sound
daily_lessons.instructions: Go on a 5-minute sound walk. Gently touch your throat while humming and pluck a stretched rubber band to feel sound moving.

daily_lessons.title: Smell & Taste Teamwork
objectives: Explore olfactory (smell) and gustatory (taste) senses
Discover how smell helps us taste food
daily_lessons.instructions: Close your eyes for the Smell Jar test. Try eating a piece of apple while holding your nose to see if taste changes.

daily_lessons.title: Touch & Sense Safety
objectives: Use skin to detect texture and temperature
Understand how senses keep us safe from dangers
daily_lessons.instructions: Reach into the Mystery Bag and guess 6 hidden items using only touch. Draw 2 ways your senses protect you (e.g., hearing a fire alarm).

daily_lessons.title: Super-Sense Animals & Review
objectives: Learn how animals use super senses to survive
Complete Week 1 Picture Quiz
daily_lessons.instructions: Pick one animal with super senses (Eagle, Dog, Bat, or Snake), present 3 fun facts to the family, and take the quiz.

questions.question: Which organ sends messages from your senses to your body?
What happens to your eye pupil in bright light?
